name: Hair-flattening bunny ears lacing

lead: Bunny ears lacing is a way of lacing a corset that combines top-down and bottom-up lacing, finishing in loops at the waist. It lets the wearer tighten or loosen the garment at the waist to shape the torso.
Corset wearers use it to get a smoother, more adjustable waist line.

paras: Corsets are usually laced at the back. In bunny ears lacing the laces run from both ends toward the middle, a method the wearer can adjust at the waist loops.
Tightening a corset compresses the torso, and strong compression has long been discussed as uncomfortable and restrictive.

angle.text: Pulling laces from both ends concentrates adjustment at the waist, which reduces the visible waist while worn.

lead: Bunny ears lacing is a corset lacing style. Corsets are typically laced at the back, and tightening or loosening the laces changes how much the garment compresses the torso. Depending on the era and effect, a corset could be laced top-down, bottom-up or both ways; the 'bunny ears' method combines the two directions [1].
The method matters for appearance because it lets the wearer control waist reduction. Historical waist reduction was likely about 5 to 15 centimetres (2 to 6 inches) [1].

paras: In the 18th century, staggered eyelets allowed spiral lacing. Metal eyelets, introduced in 1827, let wearers lace much more tightly without damaging the garment [1]. Victorian corsets added a front busk so they could be put on without re-lacing [1].

timeline.event: Metal eyelets introduced, allowing tighter lacing [1]
